description: We are a team from Kazakhstan passionate about technology, programming, and exploring our planet. We have combined our skills to create a useful and easy-to-understand project for the NASA Space Apps Challenge and show how Earth data can help us better understand the changes happening on our planet.
summary: EARTH OBSERVER is a global Earth monitoring system designed to track weather conditions, environmental changes, and natural events in real time.
details:
What it does. “Earth 2016–2026” is an interactive 3D globe showing how the planet changed over the last decade: temperature anomaly (NASA GISS), CO₂ (Mauna Loa), Arctic sea ice (NSIDC), ozone hole (NASA/NOAA Aura MLS), and key events by year. A live layer shows earthquakes (USGS, EMSC), natural events (NASA EONET, GDACS), and weather on click (Open-Meteo). A built-in viewer for NASA GIBS imagery lets users switch layers, dates, and zoom, including near-live clouds from GOES and Himawari. A “Space now” card shows an EPIC/DSCOVR image of Earth and space weather from NASA DONKI. A trend calculator (Sen’s slope, Mann-Kendall test, 95% CI) lets users test whether a change is statistically significant, and data can be downloaded as CSV.

Benefits and impact. It turns dry climate tables into an intuitive picture for students and the general public, and shows not only the trend but how reliable it is, with links to original sources.

Tools. HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript, three.js r128, Netlify Functions (proxy that keeps the NASA API key server-side), GitHub. Open APIs: NASA GIBS, EPIC, DONKI, EONET, USGS, EMSC, GDACS, Open-Meteo.

Creativity. One globe links long-term climate with what is happening right now, and lets users verify a trend with statistics instead of just reading a conclusion.

Factors considered. Scientific honesty (2026 data marked preliminary, maps labeled as illustrations, sources cited); security (strict CSP, no keys in code, external data inserted as plain text only); privacy (no cookies, no referrer sent); API load (caching, rate limits); clarity (simple interface with explanations for every layer).

AI use (for the next field): “Code, interface text, and documentation were developed and reviewed with the help of the AI assistant Claude (Anthropic) under the team’s direction. All data comes from NASA and other public APIs; AI did not generate any data.”
